explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are a large, heavy breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Kids in group I'm raising

clue.text: Ostentation of mum and son imbibing old clarets?

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so these letters go inside

explanation.surface: A mother and son flaunt themselves drinking vintage Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but means silent, as in 'keep mum'; 'imbibing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Showiness is the quality of flamboyant display, which is what ostentation means.

clue.text: I am writing brief sketches

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

explanation.surface: A comedy writer is drafting short scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims PROSE to PROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Impros are improvised pieces of comedy or drama, short unscripted sketches.

clue.text: Trees felled initially in part of S London, an annual tradition

parts.note: Tooting is a district of south London

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

explanation.surface: Cutting down trees in a London suburb has become a yearly custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes F from 'felled'; 'in' puts it inside TOOTING, a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: First-footing is the Scottish Hogmanay custom of being the first visitor across the threshold at New Year.

clue.text: French girl left in charge

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
IC stands for 'in charge', as in second-in-command

explanation.surface: A French girl has been left running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic is an adjective meaning of France, from Gaul, its Roman name.

clue.text: 50s hit — hope that will be broadcast

explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' here means scattered, not transmitted.

clue.text: Tiler misread measure

explanation.walkthrough: 'misread' rearranges TILER.

clue.text: Lady of the Lake?

explanation.surface: An allusion to the mystical figure of Arthurian legend.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Constance lies on the borders of Germany, Austria and Switzerland, and the girl's name is the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman bearing the name of a famous Alpine lake could be called this lake's lady.

clue.text: Had role right, showing supreme skill all round

indicators.note: the phrase for supreme skill goes all round the word for right, enclosing it

parts.note: top means best or supreme
OK means all right, correct
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: An actor played the part correctly, showing great skill throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' puts TOPART round OK, giving TO-OK-PART.
explanation.definitionFit: To take part is to participate, to have a role in something.

clue.text: Pronouncing short word for heart drug

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: stating means declaring or pronouncing

explanation.surface: Someone is saying aloud the abbreviated name of a cardiac medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the final G from STATING; 'word for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Statins are cholesterol-lowering medicines prescribed to cut the risk of heart disease.

clue.text: Support place for meeting south of a Manhattan thoroughfare

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so after

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a venue is where an event or meeting is held

explanation.surface: Someone backs a meeting place downtown off a New York street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' sets VENUE beneath A in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Second Avenue is a major north-south street on Manhattan's East Side.

clue.text: Transport speeds forth: he and I get bumped about, heading for terminus

indicators.note: being bumped about jostles the letters into a new order
the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'get bumped about' rearranges SPEEDS FORTH HE I into SHIPOFTHEDESER; 'heading for' takes T from 'terminus'.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is nicknamed this because it carries goods and people across sandy wastes.

clue.text: Three men regularly seen in plane perhaps

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Three men are often to be seen aboard an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T, R, E, E from 'Three men'. 'plane' is the plane tree, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a broad-leaved tree, common in city streets, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Deep ditch worker's cutting

parts.note: a trench is a long deep ditch
an ant is the crossword worker; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A labourer is digging a deep channel in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the worker ant; ''s' stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are incisive and sharp, so cutting in the figurative sense.

clue.text: The power to shift daft proposal in parliament?

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy or daft
a motion is a formal proposal put to a debating chamber

explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the ability to move from place to place.

clue.text: Header from Midlands team guy, unrelaxed

to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Header from' drops V from VILLA. Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club; 'guy' is a verb, to ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at ease is being uncomfortable or anxious, the opposite of relaxed.

clue.text: Most reliable forms of treatment received by group

indicators.note: the remedies are received inside the group's letters

parts.note: a set is a group
cures are remedies, forms of medical treatment

explanation.surface: Patients in a group are given the most dependable therapies.
explanation.definitionFit: Securest is the superlative of secure, meaning safest or most dependable.

clue.text: Consumer accepts singular diet, unusual for the time of year

indicators.note: the consumer takes in the letter for singular, holding it inside

parts.note: an eater is one who consumes
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of the word diet in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A shopper takes up a strange diet for one season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' looks like part of the dieting story but is the anagram signal; 'accepts' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastertide is the season of Easter in the church calendar, a period of the year.

clue.text: European banker entering hotel bedroom

indicators.note: the answer enters, so it lies within, the words hotel bedroom

explanation.surface: A financier from the Continent walks into a room at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elbe is a major river of Germany and the Czech Republic; a river has banks.

clue.text: Bill eco-friendly party member briefly introduced? That's right

clue.text: Traveller beginning to cost Murcian trips Trivago organised

clue.text: Foreign currency problem underpinned by the French

clue.text: Scolded group of illiterate dunces

clue.text: Writer better to leave out introduction

clue.text: Certain tradesmen for a start arranged to work together

a slow, stupid or boring person
